case_title: PRAHLAD v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.25, s.27
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the deceased had political enmity with three accused individuals, and that all three had conspired to kill the deceased. The accused used a motorcycle belonging to one of them to arrive near a bus stand where a gun shot was fired at the deceased from a short distance, resulting in his death. The charge sheet was filed, and the trial court acquitted all three accused. The High Court, however, affirmed the acquittal of one accused but convicted the other two for the offence punishable under s.302/34 IPC. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's conviction, finding the prosecution's case full of inconsistencies, contradictions, and irregularities in the investigation. The evidence of the witnesses was contradictory, and the recovery of the motorcycle and the katta were not reliable. The sole testimony of an eyewitness was not sufficient to convict the accused, and the High Court's reliance on that testimony was not justified.
